title: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
subtitle: Rich Italian risotto with golden chicken
excerpt: A deeply savoury risotto of seared chicken thigh pieces and golden chestnut mushrooms, finished with cold butter and parmesan for a creamy, restaurant-quality result. A more substantial version of the classic mushroom risotto.
sourceNotes: Chicken and mushroom risotto is a widely made combination across northern Italy, where rice has been a staple crop since the fifteenth century. The addition of chicken thigh, which stays juicy and flavourful, makes this a more complete main course than the classic version with mushrooms alone.

content.text: Sear the chicken pieces first in the same pan you will make the risotto in, then set aside and build the risotto in the same pan so the chicken juices flavour the base. This gives the final dish a much richer, more cohesive flavour than cooking them separately. Return the chicken in the last few minutes to warm through and let it finish cooking in the risotto.

items.prepNote: kept hot in a separate pan

content.text: Heat the olive oil in the large saucepan over a high heat. Season the chicken pieces and cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden. Remove and set aside.
Add the mushrooms to the same pan and cook over a high heat for 4 to 5 minutes until golden. Add the thyme and garlic, cook for 1 minute, then remove and set aside with the chicken.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Add half the butter and cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the arborio rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains are coated and just beginning to turn translucent at the edges.
Add the hot stock one ladleful at a time, waiting until each addition is absorbed before adding the next. Stir continuously. This takes 18 to 20 minutes.
When the rice has 3 minutes of cooking left, return the chicken and mushrooms to the pan. Stir gently to incorporate.
Remove from heat. Beat in the remaining cold butter and the parmesan. Rest for 2 minutes, then serve in warmed bowls scattered with parsley.

items.symptom: Chicken pieces have turned grey and steamed rather than golden.
items.cause: Pan was not hot enough or pieces were added too close together.
items.fix: Cook in a single layer over very high heat; sear do not steam.

items.symptom: Risotto is too thick and stodgy.
items.cause: Stock was added too fast, or stirring was too infrequent.
items.fix: Add stock one ladle at a time and stir steadily throughout.

items.symptom: Rice is still chalky in the centre after 20 minutes.
items.cause: Not enough stock was added or the heat was too low.
items.fix: Add more hot stock and cook for a further 3 to 5 minutes.
